content.text: topical lidocaine (or capsaicin) may be used for neuropathic pain in early CRPS w mild to moderate Sx; evidence is limited, and local burning or irritation may limit use.

Apply to intact skin over the most painful area; max 3 patches once for up to 12 h within a 24-h period. If irritation/burning occurs during application, remove patch(es) and do not reapply until irritation subsides. Avoid water contact (bathing, swimming, showering) — LIDODERM may not stick if it gets wet.
Keep out of reach of children/pets; fold used patches so adhesive sticks to itself and discard safely. CI: known Hx of sensitivity to amide-type local anesthetics or other components.

Methemoglobinemia: susceptible pts incl G6PD deficiency, congenital/idiopathic methemoglobinemia, cardiac/pulmonary compromise, infants <6 months, concurrent oxidizing agents. Immediate tx required to avert CNS/CV effects (seizures, coma, arrhythmias, death); discontinue LIDODERM and any other oxidizing agents. Even a used patch contains ≥665 mg lidocaine — small child or pet may suffer serious effects from chewing or ingesting a new or used patch. Excessive dosing (larger areas or longer than recommended wearing time) may ↑ absorption and blood concentrations → serious adverse effects. Lidocaine toxicity expected at blood concentrations above 5 mcg/mL.

Severe hepatic disease ↑ risk of toxic blood concentrations (impaired metabolism). Apply only to intact skin; application to broken/inflamed skin may ↑ blood concentrations. Use caution w Class I antiarrhythmics (tocainide, mexiletine) — toxic effects additive and potentially synergistic. OD mgmt: close monitoring, supportive care, symptomatic treatment; dialysis of negligible value.
